content.title: About
content.content: Raw mushrooms are edible fruiting bodies of various fungi, harvested from the wild or cultivated on farms. They have a delicate, slightly earthy flavor and a tender, sometimes crisp texture. Raw mushrooms are used in salads, marinades, dried as snacks, or as an ingredient in dishes that are not cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mushrooms belong to a separate kingdom of organisms, distinct from plants and animals.
There are over 10,000 edible mushroom species, but only a small fraction are widely available in stores.
Mushrooms can synthesize vitamin D2 when exposed to ultraviolet light.
Some varieties, such as button mushrooms, can be farm‑grown year‑round under controlled conditions.
Mushroom mycelium plays a key role in decomposing organic matter and maintaining soil health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Raw mushrooms provide niacin, riboflavin, thiamine, and folate, which support energy metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein source
items.content: Mushrooms deliver plant protein with few calories, making them useful for weight management.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium in mushrooms has antioxidant properties and supports immune function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High in polyphenols
items.content: Antioxidant polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Poisoning risk
items.content: Foraging wild mushrooms without proper identification can lead to consumption of toxic species.

items.title: Digestive difficulty
items.content: Some people may experience gas or stomach discomfort from raw mushrooms.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Although rare, allergies to certain mushroom varieties can occur.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Mushrooms are high in purines, which may be a concern for individuals with gout.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw mushrooms can be thinly sliced and added to salads, pickled in vinegar, used in ceviche or sushi rolls. Before eating, they should be thoroughly rinsed and, if desired, marinated to reduce any microbial risk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw mushrooms in a paper bag or a container with ventilation in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. They keep for 3‑5 days. Avoid airtight plastic bags, which accelerate spoilage.
